verdict.rationale: Isaac documents the simulation side of bring-up: importing a new robot from URDF, MJCF, Onshape CAD or USD, configuring robot and sensor models, tuning it, and writing a first standalone script to control it. It also offers Isaac ROS packages deployable on Jetson and hardware-in-the-loop testing. However, nothing in the evidence covers physical hardware drivers or real-robot configuration and first motion, and the 'hours rather than weeks' speed claim is unsupported. Missing for 10: real-hardware driver support or bring-up tooling, documented end-to-end real-robot first-motion workflow, any evidence of time-to-bring-up, independent or hands-on corroboration.
